programme.title: Damien Jurado Interview
programme.desc: Damien about how his songs come to him, Bird Tricked Into The Tree, not overthinking music, an emphasis on his vocals, producing without friend Richard Swift, his inner voice, Ochoa, the album title What’s New, Tomboy?, the characters he writes about, artists vs entertainers, connecting through music, Oh Yeah by Bo Diddley.

programme.title: Bob Mould interview
programme.desc: Bob about his early fascination with music, songs he wrote when he was 9, discovering punk rock, The Ramones and Iggy Pop, forming Hüsker Dü, gaining attention, when the band fell apart, Workbook, his time in Sugar, his parents passing, moving to Berlin, writing for Sunshine Rock.

programme.title: Cindy Blackman interview
programme.desc: Cindy about The Quarantine Blues, a chance to reset, becoming better humans, her love for the drums, always looking to improve, singing a lot on the new album Give The Drummer Some, We Came To Play, Mother Earth, sharing music, bringing jazz to more people, not putting music into boxes, inspiration, the incredible jazz musicians she learned from, enjoying the little things.

programme.title: Countain Crows interview - Adam Duritz
programme.desc: Adam about visiting his friends farm in England, shaving his head, starting on the Butter Miracle EP, music being a personal thing for him, Tall Grass, the evolution of his songwriting, the ghosts from your childhood, learning how to live, a screw-up with the release, working on a second Butter Miracle suite, keeping true to the song, a trumpet solo, the album getting so much support, feeling responsible for his crew.

programme.title: Declan McKenna interview
programme.desc: Declan about his album Zeros, finding his place in music, playfulness, making observations about society, a positive sense of humanity, Daniel You’re Still a Child, The Social Dilemma documentary, turning off his notifications, the good and bad of social media, organic and raw sounds, good mistakes, capturing the right energy on the album, trusting yourself as a musician, taking control, finally getting the album out, his favorite lyric on the album.

programme.title: Sleaford Mods with jason Part 2
programme.desc: Jason about Teacher Faces Porn Charges, starting on the album English Tapas, current affairs, a hip hop influence, getting the working class tag, humor, self-reflection, Messy Anywhere, Andrew’s beats, getting critiqued, people’s opinions, the temperament of English people, Rough Trade, their music abroad, the live shows, genuine elation, having no pretense, professionalism

programme.title: Kevin Morby interview
programme.desc: Kevin about religion, the song Beautiful Strangers, the phrase “Oh My God”, showing religion from all angles, growing up in the midwest, working with Sam Cohen again, his vocals, writing on airplanes, Hail Mary, unconventional songs, talking his time with the album, a therapeutic element, the song OMG.

programme.title: Armin van Buuren
programme.desc: Armin about always wanting his own radio show, the growth of EDM, having his own radio studio, listening to colleagues, psytrance, ‘Great Spirit’ with Vini Vici, the format for A State of Trance, the 800th episode, dreams for the future, Armin Only in the Amsterdam Arena

programme.title: Jack Savoretti interview
programme.desc: Jack about his new album Europiana, nostalgia about his childhood holidays, an education in music, finding a purpose behind what he does, scoring his second number one album, surrounding himself with the right people, writing on piano, the impact of the lockdown, working with Nile Rodgers, loving the notion of a full album, recording at Abbey Road and the magic in that studio, asking questions about true love.

programme.title: Eefje de Visser interview
programme.desc: Eefje over haar nieuwe plaat Bitterzoet, muziek voor in de auto, schrijven vanuit piano, haar thuisstudio, niet te braaf willen zijn, een internationaal gevoel, altijd beginnen bij de muziek, kritisch zijn op haar eigen teksten, beeldvorming, tegenstellingen, vluchten uit de realiteit, verloren potentie, zelf-bewustzijn, vol inspiratie zitten.

programme.title: The Drums
programme.desc: An Interview with The Drums

programme.title: John Petrucci interview
programme.desc: John about his continuing love for the guitar, looking at his own music objectively, challenging himself, working on Terminal Velocity, playing the blues, Out of the Blue, making a style your own, the song Terminal Velocity, relearning Gemini, playing with Dave LaRue and Mike Portnoy, his old drumkit, putting the album out on his own label, learning more about the business, the impact of Eddie van Halen.

programme.title: Animal Collective interview - Panda Bear
programme.desc: Noah about injuring his finger, how the Animal Collective got started, why he makes music, his creative process, the beginnings of Time Skiffs, working in service of the songs, shaping the arrangements, being guarded about lyrics, Prester John, Car Keys, a backwards album cycle, a crossroads for the music industry, naming the album ‘Time Skiffs'

programme.title: Big Thief interview - Adrienne Lenker
programme.desc: Adrianne about curiosity, a sense of stillness, creativity and songwriting, music as a bridge to the etherial world, tapping into inspiration, why we do what we do, starting on the new album U.F.O.F, dealing with success, keeping a connection with yourself as you evolve, wanting to be part of something bigger, how the band was formed, the album title, alienation in society, sharing her art.

programme.title: Death Angel interview - Ted Aguilar
programme.desc: Ted about being a Death Angel fan from day 1, coming up in the Bay Area trash scene, how he got into music, joining Death Angel, his first shows with the band, perseverance and the love for playing music, The Bastard Tracks, his favorite live tracks, rare live tracks, the challenges with Frolic Through the Park, acoustic songs, his thoughts on Rob and Mark’s lyrics, Tom Petty, working on a new Death Angel album, not being able to tour, adapting to a changing industry.

programme.title: Marlon Williams interview
programme.desc: Marlon about touring with Lorde, dabbling in acting, the start of My Boy, being judged publicly, eclectic songwriting, the song My Boy, simplicity in his writing, Māori strumming, Don’t Go Back, finding a healthy work/life balance, Thinking of Nina, Soft Boys Make The Grade

programme.title: David Paich interview
programme.desc: David about writing poems as a child, Elton John, Houston I’m Coming To See You, forming Toto, Hold The Line, Rosanna, track splicing and modern production, working on The Girl Is Mine, Forgotten Toys, Queen Charade, Forward, Willibelongtoyou, Spirit of the Moonrise, All The Tears That Shine

programme.title: Jinjer interview - Tatiana and Eugene
programme.desc: Tatiana and Eugene rising in popularity, releasing the new album Wallflowers, adjust to life without touring, music as escapism, the writing process, working on the sound of the new album, Tatiana needing pressure to write lyrics, being a live-oriented band, high-flowing poetry, improvising with vocals, personal lyrics, Copycat and authenticity in art, creating something of your own

programme.title: Tom Chaplin interview
programme.desc: Tom about climate change, a new attitude to living, parenthood and growing older, asking yourself the difficult questions, happiness not being a destination, not fitting in as a teenager and dealing with negative emotions, Stars Align and working with Ethan Johns, electronic sounds, Gonna Run, brutally honest lyrics, the road he has traveled, Overshoot

programme.title: Destroyer interview - Dan Bejar
programme.desc: Dan about film scores, when he became obsessed with songwriting, instrumental music, using the original vocal tapes, Crimson Tide, lyrics and sounds, The Television Music Supervisor, a collective process, Cue Synthesizer, his musical identity, figuring out how to play the record live, the title Have We Met.

programme.title: St. Vincent interview
programme.desc: Annie about how she started in music, creative expression, the sound of the early 70s, writing for her new album Daddy’s Home, writing about flawed people, Somebody Like Me, finding stillness for the first time, not worrying about the commercial side, signing an autograph in prison, why she decided to write about the incarceration of her father, the Wurlitzer, working with Jack Antonoff, the various ways of writing songs, knowing when a song is done, performing at SNL.

programme.title: Jean-Michel Jarre interview
programme.desc: Jean-Michel about Welcome To The Other Side, a virtual Notre Dame, the impact of the pandemic on music, innovations in music technology, binaural recording, VR and augmented reality as new forms of expression, the value of music, respecting intellectual property, this being only the beginning of the digital age, artificial intelligence, Ray Charles and Pierre Soulages, lessons from his mother, a street in Lyon being named after his mother

programme.title: Between The Buried And Me interview - Dustie Waring
programme.desc: Dustie about his mindset around the first Colors album, never repeating themselves, songs that are difficult to play, pushing themselves, working on Colors II during the pandemic, writing the album over the internet, a collective writing approach, believing in albums, being proud of what you create, preparing for live shows, art that takes risks, creative freedom, bands that last.

programme.title: Glass Animals interview - Joe Seaward
programme.desc: Joe about gearing up towards the third album Dreamland, suffering a terrible accident, a time for reflection, not taking things for granted, finding out who the people around you really are, the first rehearsal after the accident, the songwriting for Dreamland, Your Love, how he connects with all of the songs on the album, songs that make you feel, not being able to tour the album, finding new ways to present the album.

programme.title: DMA's interview - Tommy O'Dell
programme.desc: Tommy about their show at the Brixton Academy and Liam Gallagher, finding his voice, the album Glow, dance elements, writing lyrics, Silver, staying true to yourself, ambition, not trying to please everyone, Never Before, Criminals and pop, songs that evolve on the road, Life is a Game of Changing, what he learned as a frontman.

programme.title: Katie Melua interview
programme.desc: Katie about her new album No. 8, playing the entire album live, Remind Me To Forget, her first studio album without Mike Batt, changing things up, celebrating great musicianship, working with producer Leo Abrahams, developing as a songwriter, English Manner, her divorce, love propaganda, focusing on what’s important, being adventurous, getting into photography.

programme.title: Joe Satriani interview
programme.desc: Joe about when he was still a beginner on guitar, working hard to get better, NYC in the early 70s, the surrealness of his career, teaching Steve Vai, finding “work-arounds” as a guitar player, Eddie van Halen, The Elephants of Mars, experimentation, composing songs over the internet, songs coming together organically, a song inspired by Questlove, Randy Rhoads and what keeps inspiring him.

programme.title: Declan McKenna interview
programme.desc: Declan about political engagement, making people think, The Kids Don’t Wanna Come Home, confusion, younger generations, his first songs, rowdy live shows, winning over crowds, a sold-out tour, his upcoming debut record, growing as a songwriter

programme.title: DMA's interview - Johnny Took
programme.desc: Johnny about the past 2 years, their loyal fans, early influences and genre-blending, the evolution of their sound, having loads of time in the studio, shaping How Many Dreams?, I Don’t Need To Hide, creating a dynamic live show, old vs new songs, De Carle and pushing boundaries

programme.title: Band of Horses interview - Ben Bridwell
programme.desc: Ben about needing a change, taking a stab at producing the album, the sound of Things Are Great, making a connection, sounding more like himself, Warning Signs, having success, struggling during lockdown, his love for songwriting, being a conduit for songs, being a fan of music first, trusting himself.

programme.title: Myles Kennedy interview
programme.desc: Myles about a road trip through America, getting out of your bubble, his new solo album The Ides of March, slide guitar, the Sifting Through The Fire intro, making sense of the world and songwriting, Get Along, playing the blues, Love Rain Down, the title track, uncertainty about the future, affecting people with music, the need to create, and a lot more! (11/05/2021)

programme.title: Agnes Obel interview
programme.desc: Agnes about playing piano at an early age, starting to write her own songs, lyrics. and melodies, tapping into the stream of inspiration, a great sense of freedom, Myopia, Camera’s Rolling, playing with pitch, knowing when you’re on the right track, experimenting with her voice, vocals vs instrumentals

programme.title: Shaggy interview
programme.desc: Shaggy about his earliest Christmas memories, Raggamuffin Christmas, having good people around you, becoming a brand, why he got into music, welcoming change, always wanting to learn, how the Christmas In The Islands, album got started, Caribbean Christmas parties, the cultural impact of Jamaica, affecting people in a positive way, his favorite live act, what inspires his songwriting, music for the right mood, Bob Marley.

programme.title: The Head And The Heart with Jonathan and Kenny Part 1
SIXX:A.M. interview - James Michael
programme.desc: James about being an observer of life, memories of his childhood, music production back in the day, modern production techniques, the HITS album, maintaining a sense of innocence, living out his rock star dreams, dealing with public notoriety, all having their favorite SIXX:A.M. albums and songs, talking about substance abuse, the connection with their fans, the power and importance of music, music as comfort food, Bat Out Of Hell.

programme.title: Alain Clark interview
programme.desc: Alain over echte connecties maken, de iPad generatie, Sunday Afternoon, de afstand met z’n publiek verkleinen, Michael Jackson, een echo van Bad Therapy, schrijven wat hij voelt, samenwerkingen, kwetsbaarheid en eerlijkheid, Song’s Don’t Die, Joni Mitchell, mensen raken met z’n muziek, clubshows op zondagmiddag

programme.title: Gilbert O'Sullivan interview
programme.desc: Gilbert about performing live, why he started writing songs, The Beatles, the first song he was proud of, Alone Again (naturally), his creative process, the new album Driven and writing melodies, the art of songwriting, working with Mick Hucknall and KT Tunstall, keeping up with modern music, a misunderstood song, the drive to create

programme.title: Floor Jansen interview
programme.desc: Floor about developing her solo career, finding her own sound, her approach to songwriting, Fire, staying connected with her fans, showing her personality on social media, Tuomas’ writing and her own creative expression, working towards an album, new Nightwish songs, still growing as a vocalist, participating in ‘Sing Meinen Song’

programme.title: The Lumineers interview - Wesley Schultz and Jermiah Fraites
programme.desc: Wesley and Jeremiah about Cleopatra, something they learned from U2, how we connect to music, transcending generations, album III, opening up to others, taking the stigma away from addiction, difficult subjects, Gloria, Kurt Cobain, sadness and beauty, telling the truth about addiction, the identities of all their albums, how they see succes, playing the long game, what makes a good song.

programme.title: Bombay Bicycle Club interview - Ed and Jack
programme.desc: Ed and Jack about taking a break, Ed’s solo record, Mr Jukes, a life outside of music, getting back together, writing for Everything Else Has Gone Wrong, Ed contributing songs, the title track, Good Day, instagram culture, growing as people, optimism, striving for improvement.

programme.title: The Kills interview - Alison Mosshart and Jamie Hince
programme.desc: Alison and Jamie about the impact of the pandemic on their industry, a desire for live music, reminiscing with the Little Bastards album, their early tours, leaf blower interruptions, bizarre live shows, the magic of youthful nativity, imposter syndrome, Raise Me, a DIY approach, how the notion of success has changed, working on a new album.

programme.title: AWOLNATION interview - Aaron Bruno
programme.desc: Aaron about Gilbert O’Sullivan’s Alone Again (Naturally), covering well-known songs on ‘My Echo, My Shadow, My Covers, and Me’, music as an escape, Take A Chance On Me, learning from covering songs, picking who to collaborate with, how he writes music, tours that never happened, writing new material, covers and memes of his own song

programme.title: JP Cooper interview
programme.desc: JP about comparing his new album 'She' to his debut album, putting more of himself in the songs, success and imposter syndrome, multiple versions of the same song, how he writes songs, the lyrics, Bits and Pieces, making a connection with his audience, music he listens to himself, the women in his life, taking the good with the bad, healing through songwriting, how he looks at success these days.

programme.title: Benny Sings
programme.desc: Benny about his early band Love Boat, why he started singing, Champagne People, what makes music great, City Pop, what drives him, Everything I Know, writing about Love, his connection with Japan.

programme.title: Nightwish interview - Troy Donockley
programme.desc: Troy about getting sucked into metal, creating textures, pushing the Uilleann pipes to their extremes, singing on Harvest, engaging with life, his custom-made set of pipes, being in awe of nature, the magic of music, entertainment vs self-discovery, being proud of the new album Human. :|: Nature.

programme.title: Alvaro Soler interview
programme.desc: Álvaro about his early beginnings in music, moving to Japan as a kid, finding confidence in himself, finding his musical identity, becoming the center of attention, dealing with success, starting on Mar de Colores, music for every situation, knowing when a song will work, La Cintura and La Libertad, growing as a person

programme.title: Japanese Breakfast interview - Michelle Zauner
programme.desc: Michelle about writing her book ‘Crying in H Mart: A Memoir’ vs writing a song, writing about something new on her new album Jubilee, 2019 being a good year for her, self-imposed pressure, why people might like her music, Posing In Bondage, Kokomo Indiana, delving into the Beatles, her thoughts on success.

programme.title: Franz Ferdinand interview - Alex Kapranos at Lowlands
programme.desc: Alex about The Yummy Fur, the evolution of the band, working with Sparks, recording songs quickly, band chemistry, getting his break in his 30s, The Beatles, knowing when a song is good, an emotional reward, Always Ascending, Live and Let Die.

programme.title: Lost Frequencies interview - Felix De Laet
programme.desc: Felix about the title of most booked festival artist, how he looks back at his success so far, developing his live show, the keytar and learning to play the guitar, connecting with people while on stage, the type of tracks he’s been producing during lockdown, learning from a Major Lazer remix, Rise, achieving his dreams, exploring new music, what comes next.

programme.title: Monster Magnet interview - Dave Wyndorf
programme.desc: Dave about music in the 60s, the language of counterculture, an amazing fuzz tone, how music is remembered, Hawkwind and bands that deserve more recognition, making a deal with the devil, the band Table Scraps, shaping the album Better Dystopia, art in the internet world, capturing the right sound, Jack White, learning about his voice, Dust’s Learning to Die, dealing with the lockdowns, live music in the 70s, talking vs listening, music as a transportive experience, commenting about society, how musicians get paid, hope for the future, the era of infotainment.

programme.title: Max Cavalera interview
programme.desc: Max about the music his parents played when he was young, bossanova and Opera, his artistic side, finding heavy metal at the right time, a gift for writing angry songs, protecting his rebellious side, a song about cancer, Totem, native tribes in North America, ancestors, Marc Rizzo leaving the band, Eddie van Halen, Cavalera Conspiracy, playing with his brother Igor, revisiting Sepultura albums

programme.title: Steve Lukather interview
programme.desc: Steve about being stuck at home, how I Found The Sun Again got made, where his passion for music comes from, Toto, Weezer’s cover of Toto, re-creating the 70s live sound, his admiration for George Harrison, getting anger out through a song, losing his best friends, why he got sober, his autistic son, Joe Walsh and Steve Winwood, capturing a real performance, worries about Covid-19, the longevity of Toto, working with Paul McCartney.

programme.title: Ayreon interview - Arjen Lucassen
programme.desc: Arjen about Eddie van Halen, the rock & roll lifestyle, what he has learned from his previous albums, taking risks, the beginning of Transitus, starting with the story, John Carpenter, finding the right vocalists, ghost movies, the plot of Transitus, shorter songs, Tom Baker and Doctor Who, working with his heroes, Dee Snider, how Joe Satriani got involved, Marty Friedman’s guitar skills, casting Tommy Karevik and Simone Simons, doing everything different, trying to get the movie made with Dick Maas, performing live.

programme.title: Jerry Cantrell and Tyyler Bates interview
programme.desc: Jerry and Tyler about the John Wick 2 OST, the start of Brighten, their creative process together, using his time outside of Alice in Chains well, darkness and glimmers of hope, writing lyrics, letting the art speak for itself, having two drummers on the album, Greg Puciato’s harmonies, Travis’ thoughts on Alice in Chains, Jerry looking back at his early career, songs that defined the Alice in Chains sound.

programme.title: Beth Hart interview
programme.desc: Beth about learning from gardening, magical moments, addressing personal issues, facing your problems and taking responsibility, singing Led Zeppelin songs, healing through music, recording vocals, Stairway To Heaven and No Quarter, getting honest feedback, other artists she would like to cover, writing new songs of her own, trying new things, being willing to fail and learn, her love for the Netherlands.

programme.title: Wardruna interview - Einar Selvik (2021)
programme.desc: Einar about hunting for songs, inspiration in nature, not wanting to repeat himself, the influence of Skald on the new record, building a strong foundation of knowledge, a multi-disciplinary approach, highlighting the things that universally resonate with people, learning from the past, the album Kvitravn, how he writes his songs, the title track, a flock of ravens around his house, letting a song be what it is, live performances, working on the Assassins Creed Valhalla game, how we remember history.

programme.title: Eivør interview
programme.desc: Eivør about growing up in a secluded place, being close to nature, electronic and organic sounds, how she starts on a new album, the new album Segl, her creative force, opening up for collaborations, Only Love with Ásgeir, Let It Come, listening to your inner voice, contrasts, a crossroads in her life, creative freedom, the title Segl (sail), hope, Patience, making people feel something.

programme.title: Bennie Jolink interview
programme.desc: Bennie over z’n liefde voor tekenen, beginnen aan de nieuwe plaat en boek Bernard Jolink: Post Normaal, hoe muziek in z’n leven kwam, het op z’n eigen manier doen, success, het eerste grote optreden met Normaal, waarom boerenrock aansloeg, een rel bij TopPop, eigenwijsheid, Ik Goa Mien Eigen Gang, schrijven met Alan Gascoigne, Jamaica, jezelf niet te serieus nemen, roem, gezondheidsproblemen, Ij Moet Deur, moderne muziek, muziek dat hem raakt, Kameraad, z’n vriendschap met Jan Manschot, z’n allerlaatste optreden

programme.title: Five Finger Death Punch interview - Zoltan Bathory
programme.desc: Zoltan about being forced to take a break, what drives him, living life to the fullest, manifesting thoughts, wanting to be an astronaut, getting started on AfterLife, the band being polarizing, success and envy, fresh energy in the band, true creative freedom, the concept of AfterLife, a cultural paradigm shift, near-death experiences, spirituality, Judgement Day.

programme.title: Daughtry interview - Chris Daughtry
programme.desc: Chris about Heavy Is The Crown, the most liberating album he’s made, starting again from the ground up, going independent, the writing process for World On Fire, challenging himself vocally, finding his voice, Chris Cornell and covering ‘Hunger Strike’, going sober, mental health, dealing with his struggles through song.

programme.title: Sleaford Mods with jason Part 1
programme.desc: Jason about Teacher Faces Porn Charges, starting on the album English Tapas, current affairs, a hip hop influence, getting the working class tag, humor, self-reflection, Messy Anywhere, Andrew’s beats, getting critiqued, people’s opinions, the temperament of English people, Rough Trade, their music abroad, the live shows, genuine elation, having no pretense, professionalism

programme.title: Alt-J interview - Thom Sonny Green
programme.desc: Thom about taking a year off, getting ready for The Dream, Walk a Mile, having no expectations for the new album, channeling his feelings into music, Shakespeare, his passion for art, Philadelphia, their growing friendship within the band, Get Better, field recordings and playing with sound, thinking about another solo album.

programme.title: Damien Jurado Interview
programme.desc: Damien about how his songs come to him, Bird Tricked Into The Tree, not overthinking music, an emphasis on his vocals, producing without friend Richard Swift, his inner voice, Ochoa, the album title What’s New, Tomboy?, the characters he writes about, artists vs entertainers, connecting through music, Oh Yeah by Bo Diddley.

programme.title: Bob Mould interview
programme.desc: Bob about his early fascination with music, songs he wrote when he was 9, discovering punk rock, The Ramones and Iggy Pop, forming Hüsker Dü, gaining attention, when the band fell apart, Workbook, his time in Sugar, his parents passing, moving to Berlin, writing for Sunshine Rock.

programme.title: Cindy Blackman interview
programme.desc: Cindy about The Quarantine Blues, a chance to reset, becoming better humans, her love for the drums, always looking to improve, singing a lot on the new album Give The Drummer Some, We Came To Play, Mother Earth, sharing music, bringing jazz to more people, not putting music into boxes, inspiration, the incredible jazz musicians she learned from, enjoying the little things.

programme.title: Countain Crows interview - Adam Duritz
programme.desc: Adam about visiting his friends farm in England, shaving his head, starting on the Butter Miracle EP, music being a personal thing for him, Tall Grass, the evolution of his songwriting, the ghosts from your childhood, learning how to live, a screw-up with the release, working on a second Butter Miracle suite, keeping true to the song, a trumpet solo, the album getting so much support, feeling responsible for his crew.

programme.title: Declan McKenna interview
programme.desc: Declan about his album Zeros, finding his place in music, playfulness, making observations about society, a positive sense of humanity, Daniel You’re Still a Child, The Social Dilemma documentary, turning off his notifications, the good and bad of social media, organic and raw sounds, good mistakes, capturing the right energy on the album, trusting yourself as a musician, taking control, finally getting the album out, his favorite lyric on the album.

programme.title: Sleaford Mods with jason Part 2
programme.desc: Jason about Teacher Faces Porn Charges, starting on the album English Tapas, current affairs, a hip hop influence, getting the working class tag, humor, self-reflection, Messy Anywhere, Andrew’s beats, getting critiqued, people’s opinions, the temperament of English people, Rough Trade, their music abroad, the live shows, genuine elation, having no pretense, professionalism

programme.title: Kevin Morby interview
programme.desc: Kevin about religion, the song Beautiful Strangers, the phrase “Oh My God”, showing religion from all angles, growing up in the midwest, working with Sam Cohen again, his vocals, writing on airplanes, Hail Mary, unconventional songs, talking his time with the album, a therapeutic element, the song OMG.

programme.title: Armin van Buuren
programme.desc: Armin about always wanting his own radio show, the growth of EDM, having his own radio studio, listening to colleagues, psytrance, ‘Great Spirit’ with Vini Vici, the format for A State of Trance, the 800th episode, dreams for the future, Armin Only in the Amsterdam Arena

programme.title: Jack Savoretti interview
programme.desc: Jack about his new album Europiana, nostalgia about his childhood holidays, an education in music, finding a purpose behind what he does, scoring his second number one album, surrounding himself with the right people, writing on piano, the impact of the lockdown, working with Nile Rodgers, loving the notion of a full album, recording at Abbey Road and the magic in that studio, asking questions about true love.

programme.title: Eefje de Visser interview
programme.desc: Eefje over haar nieuwe plaat Bitterzoet, muziek voor in de auto, schrijven vanuit piano, haar thuisstudio, niet te braaf willen zijn, een internationaal gevoel, altijd beginnen bij de muziek, kritisch zijn op haar eigen teksten, beeldvorming, tegenstellingen, vluchten uit de realiteit, verloren potentie, zelf-bewustzijn, vol inspiratie zitten.

programme.title: Princess Play Time
programme.desc: The proud Princess likes to do things her own way, but her antics are always joined by her restless brother, Prince, who tends to turn everything topsy-turvy. Any playtime in their room transforms into a fantastic journey through unusual worlds: the children arrange a picnic on the Moon, conduct a detective investigation in a toy city, or search for pirate treasures on islands! Although initially, the Princess and Prince seem to clash and compete, by the end, they always find joy in each other's company and that of their cherished dog, Bona.

But even masters need to stop and refuel. When meals or snack time interrupt Ollie’s play, he finds himself confronted with the real challenge of childhood; trying new food. To escape his predicament, Ollie uses his magic spoon to transport himself, along with his sister Poppy, and her stuffy Nummy, to a food planet filled with adventure and the very food Ollie stuck his spoon into.

programme.title: Insight with Haslinda Amin
programme.desc: In a volatile and unpredictable world, the show will be the definitive guide for the global news audience to get the complete picture on the biggest story of the day. With news making executives, officials and thought-leaders from the world of business, politics and academia we will explore a story through probing interviews and nuanced conversations. The hour of programming will also highlight the most relevant stories from India which is currently one of the hottest investment destinations, but also has compelling stories that play into the Bloomberg's priority issues such as Climate change, Diversity and Technological innovation.

programme.title: Bloomberg Horizons Middle East & Africa
programme.desc: A spotlight on the fast paced growth and major deals happening across the Middle East and Africa. Linking the market drivers from overnight in the US and across Asia into the region's trading day, with deep dive analysis of the top business, energy and geopolitical stories shaping the decisions of traders across the Middle East, Africa and beyond.

programme.title: Bloomberg Daybreak Europe
programme.desc: Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. Live from London, we set the agenda for your day, catching you up with overnight markets news from the US and Asia. And we'll tell you what matters for investors in Europe, giving you insight before trading begins.

programme.title: Bloomberg The Opening Trade
programme.desc: The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game.

programme.title: The Pulse with Francine Lacqua
programme.desc: The Pulse with Francine Lacqua is all about conversations with high profile guests in the beating heart of global business, economics, finance and politics. Based in London, we go wherever the story is, bringing you exclusive interviews and market-moving scoops.

programme.title: Bloomberg Brief
programme.desc: Bloomberg Brief delivers the market news, data and analysis you need to set your agenda.

programme.title: Bloomberg Surveillance
programme.desc: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern have the economy and global markets "under surveillance". Their daily conversations with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond cover the latest in business, investment, and geopolitics. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day.

programme.title: Bloomberg Open Interest
programme.desc: Bloomberg Open Interest with Matt Miller and Dani Burger — delivers the market-moving news you need to know to get a jump start on the US trading day.

programme.title: Bloomberg Tech
programme.desc: Bloomberg Tech is the only daily live technology program with a focus on breaking news, market-moving reporting and analysis of global technology companies and stories. The program brings the audience interviews from the biggest names in the business, offering in-depth analysis and critical insights.

programme.title: Bloomberg Money
programme.desc: Tom Keene and Scarlet Fu explore how people earn, spend, and build wealth — with smart insights and reporting to help viewers navigate their financial futures.

programme.title: Bloomberg Balance of Power
programme.desc: Bloomberg Balance of Power focuses on politics and policies on Capitol Hill, in President Trump's administration, the federal agencies and the courts.

programme.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily
programme.desc: Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec bring you reporting from the magazine that helps global leaders stay ahead, plus insight on the people, companies and trends shaping today's complex economy.

programme.title: Bloomberg The Close
programme.desc: Romaine Bostick and Katie Greifeld break down the day's top market-moving stories and trading action around the closing bell.

programme.title: The Amazon Divide
programme.desc: While Brazil boasts falling deforestation rates, woodlands just across the border in Bolivia are vanishing faster than ever. Bloomberg Originals traces how the practices that created Mato Grosso, Brazil’s agricultural heartland, are spilling into San Ignacio, Bolivia’s fastest-growing deforestation hotspot, and asks a simple question: what if preservation efforts in one country simply displace development to another?

programme.title: BizPodcast: What surprises foreign journalists most about China?
programme.desc: What surprises and impresses foreign journalists the most when they visit China? Which stories about China are they most eager to share with audiences back home? What expectations do they have for the upcoming China International Import Expo? Tune in to our podcast to discover their experiences, and hear fresh perspectives and untold stories from China!

programme.title: Live promo: Small products, big industry: Meet the Canton Fair's manufacturing 'hidden champions'
programme.desc: At the 140th Canton Fair on Saturday, CGTN reporter He Jingyi joins Johann Anton Klimmer, a German tool importer and longtime Canton Fair buyer, to explore specialized sectors ranging from hardware and tools to precision components, general machinery, and lighting and electrical products. These specialized SMEs may not be household names, but their smart manufacturing capabilities, comprehensive industrial support and resilient supply chains are a vital source of strength for China's manufacturing sector - and help keep global production moving. What can seemingly ordinary products tell us about the strength of a much larger industry?

programme.title: Dubai Chambers chairman: Chinese innovation is very welcome in Dubai
programme.desc: Dubai is already home to over 6,600 Chinese companies, but the emirate wants to see more. programme.title: Global Business-Asian Edition Ep.2
programme.desc: Global Business is the flagship business show of CGTN English Channel, bringing you the latest economic data, business trends and policies.

programme.title: 140th Canton Fair - machines built to work with humans
programme.desc: Seventy years ago, the Canton Fair featured Chinese tea, silk and handmade goods. Today, it's about robots. Join us to see dexterous robotic hands, exoskeletons and companion robots, and how AI works alongside humans.

programme.title: How China's ocean kingdom makes billions
programme.desc: In Southern China, a theme park you've likely never heard of is attracting more annual visitors than Hollywood Universal. The question is, how? Meet Chimelong Ocean Kingdom. It holds seven Guinness World Records and features the largest aquarium on earth. CGTN's Yu Hongyu dives into the strategy behind the splash to see how a local park created a hundred-billion-dollar opportunity.

programme.title: China's Kungfu theme park: A wild ride back in time
programme.desc: At Wansuishan Martial Arts City in central China’s Kaifeng, Henan Province, you’re not just a visitor - you’re part of the story. Every segment in the park is part of an immersive experience rooted in Chinese martial arts and traditional culture. From live matchmaking shows to iron flower performances, from Song Dynasty streets to interactive stages, this uniquely Chinese theme park – with not even one roller coaster or scary ride – was able to record over 24 million visits in 2025.

programme.title: Bizfocus: From myth to reality: How tech brings Eastern imagination to life
programme.desc: Ever wondered what China’s version of “Adam and Eve” or “Beauty and the Beast” looks like? While the world’s theme parks are all about Western fairy tales, one Chinese park took a different path—Fantawild brings ancient Eastern myths to life with mind-blowing tech and art. In this episode of Bizfocus, CGTN’s Xu Yi and her new friends from Pakistan and Bangladesh go for adventure in Fantawild Oriental Heritage in Mianyang, Sichuan. Gods, legends, and the tech behind the magic—all in one epic trip.

programme.title: BEYOND CHINA'S Q3 ECONOMY AND 2026 OUTLOOK
programme.desc: China's economy has maintained steady performance amid strong resilience and vitality. Biztalk host Guan Xin speaks to leading economists and analysts to decipher the drive toward new growth and the accelerated advancement of structural upgrading and look ahead to the next stage of China's economy.

programme.title: China-US partnerships fueling rapid growth
programme.desc: Starbucks landed in China when coffee was a novelty. Today, 1 in 5 stores globally is there. American fast food and retail giants placed the same bet, and cashed in. Now local brands are out-executing them. The fix? Partner with Chinese private equity. Here's why it's working, and what it means for both sides.

programme.title: The green bridge between China & US
programme.desc: In 2019, Tesla was running on fumes. Shanghai handed it a lifeline, a gigafactory built in 10 months. Today, that plant produces nearly half of all Teslas using 95% local parts. That same playbook is expanding across green tech, pairing Chinese battery tech with American software. When the world's two largest economies build together, clean energy gets cheaper and faster for everyone.

programme.title: China-US: The efficiency advantage
programme.desc: The iPhone in your pocket? A global masterpiece. Apple's supply chain spans the world, with America's design expertise meeting China's manufacturing strength. Precision, speed and scale turn bold ideas into products in your hands. And this goes beyond Apple: cooperation across borders can drive innovation and growth. When the world's two biggest economies click, everyone benefits.

programme.desc: In this special series, "China's Economy and the World," expert Sławomir Majman, Vice President of the Polish Institute of Security and International Development and former President of the Polish Information and Foreign Investment Agency, explores China's 15th Five-Year Plan and the reshaping global economic order.

programme.title: Live promo: Small products, big industry: Meet the Canton Fair's manufacturing 'hidden champions'
programme.desc: At the 140th Canton Fair on Saturday, CGTN reporter He Jingyi joins Johann Anton Klimmer, a German tool importer and longtime Canton Fair buyer, to explore specialized sectors ranging from hardware and tools to precision components, general machinery, and lighting and electrical products. These specialized SMEs may not be household names, but their smart manufacturing capabilities, comprehensive industrial support and resilient supply chains are a vital source of strength for China's manufacturing sector - and help keep global production moving. What can seemingly ordinary products tell us about the strength of a much larger industry?

programme.title: Global Business-American Edition Ep.2

programme.title: Dubai Chambers chairman: Chinese innovation is very welcome in Dubai
programme.desc: Dubai is already home to over 6,600 Chinese companies, but the emirate wants to see more. programme.title: Live: Canton Fair's 'hidden champions' - small firms, global reach

programme.title: China Agenda 2026
programme.desc: Special coverage of China's annual sessions of its top legislature and political advisory body, known as the "Two Sessions".

programme.title: China's concert boom: Why Gen Z is filling the stadiums
programme.desc:
From packed stadium shows to sold-out performances in smaller cities, China's live music scene is expanding rapidly. Young audiences are turning concerts into a cultural routine: traveling across cities, sharing the experience online and building collective memories around live performances.
The boom now extends far beyond the stage, boosting tourism, retail spending and local economies. In this episode of Unboxing China, we explore how concerts are reshaping consumption patterns and becoming a new driver of cultural and urban development.

programme.title: The self-care economy explained: How emotional spending is reshaping consumer trends
programme.desc:
For months, Chinese social feeds have been filled with "Lao Ji"- a third-person way of saying "me." What began as a slang sign-off, "Love you, Lao Ji. See you tomorrow," now signals a broader shift toward self-care and emotional self-support. It also feeds a huge market where young consumers are rechanneling budgets toward small, meaningful purchases that support emotional wellbeing.
In this episode of Unboxing China, we trace how a casual phrase turned into a cultural movement, reshaping consumption and mental-health talk.

programme.title: Inside China's Q3 Economy
programme.desc: China's economy expanded 4.6% in the first three quarters, with exports and high-tech manufacturing continuing to provide support, while consumption and industrial output picked up in September. What do the latest numbers reveal about China's growth momentum and economic transformation? Can renewed momentum and an improved structure help sustain growth in the months ahead? Join BizTalk as leading economists and experts take a closer look at China's Q3 economic performance, unpack the key signals behind the headline numbers, and assess the outlook for growth.

programme.title: Adidas CEO: Competition with Chinese brands makes us better
programme.desc: German sportswear giant Adidas has been in China for decades, but it's no longer just selling a European playbook. Its "In China, For China" model puts designers, creatives and supply chains directly into the bustle of the world's second largest economy - where competition is fierce and Chinese sportswear brands are stronger than ever. Recently in Shanghai, CGTN reporter Wang Tianyu caught up with Adidas global CEO Bjørn Gulden to find out more.

programme.title: 1st Bite
programme.desc: Set on a tropical island in Thailand, the strange plight of a beleaguered chef who, while romancing a mysterious woman, discovers the diabolical Zen of cooking. Following a near death escape, he returns to Montreal and falls hard for the woman of his life who unfortunately craves only his cooking but not his loving. Worse still, strange things surfacing around him indicate that his journey to the Far East has deep, divine implications. The stage is set for him to take the 1st bite of true love and end the cycle of suffering for all involved.

programme.title: Frank & Fearless
programme.desc: An aging reprobate, a rural boy, a large dog and an orphaned baby rhino set out to stop the rhino slaughter. Their quest buffets them between high comedy and searing tragedy, until they end up an inspiration and a conscience to a world in need of heroes.

programme.title: Gumshoe
programme.desc: When hopeless New Orleans private eye Biff Basham is hired by a seductive nightclub singer to pay off a blackmailer, he thinks his money worries are over. But when his client's husband is murdered, he is plunged into a dangerous world of organized crime and espionage in this zany comedy. Can Biff unmask the killer before he becomes the next victim?

programme.title: Nothing Good Ever Happens
programme.desc: Neil who is a painter and graphic designer, on a morning just like any other morning his girlfriend Amanda leaves him and moves out of their house (don't worry, it's a rental.) That morning Neil tries to cope as best he knows how, but in a strange turn of events he ends up shooting back a glass of bleach. He wakes up to suicide watch and court appointed therapy as well as the empty void Amanda left. Now Neil has to decide what he can do to feel better about himself. Should he get Amanda back? Make his old friends like him again? Confront his estranged father? Eat a ton of Chinese food? Or maybe he should just finish his latest goddamned painting.

programme.title: Killer Drag Queens On Dope
programme.desc: Killer Drag Queens on Dope! is the wild story of Ginger & Coco, two dolls with a little secret... They're contract killers who work for a one-eyed lunatic named Uncle A. Half the cutthroats in town are trying to kill them, the other half are trying to sleep with them and Uncle A is just getting started. Ginger is hell on heels. Coco never met a drug she didn't like. Together, they're Killer Drag Queens on Dope!

programme.title: FUNDADORAS | Miriam de Paoli: romper tabúes sobre la menopausia con No Pausa.
programme.desc: "La menopausia no es una enfermedad. Es una etapa natural de nuestras vidas." En este nuevo episodio de Fundadoras, Sabrina Díaz Ibarra conversa con Miriam de Paoli, fundadora de No Pausa, periodista, innovadora social y referente en longevidad y salud femenina. ¿Qué pasa cuando una mujer tarda más de un año en recibir un diagnóstico para una etapa natural como el climaterio? ¿Por qué seguimos en silencio sobre la menopausia? ¿Cómo pueden la tecnología, los datos y la comunidad cambiarlo todo? Una charla poderosa sobre romper tabúes, emprender con propósito y construir un futuro más inclusivo para las mujeres. Suscribite al canal y activá la campanita para más entrevistas con mujeres que están transformando el mundo. Encontranos también en Instagram y LinkedIn como @sabrinadiazibarra #Fundadoras #NoPausa #MiriamDePaoli #Menopausia #SaludFemenina #Longevidad #Climaterio #InnovaciónSocial

programme.title: FUNDADORAS | Entrevista a Helena Estrada
programme.desc: En esta conversación, Helena Estrada nos comparte su visión sobre el liderazgo femenino, la independencia financiera y el poder de tomar las riendas de nuestra vida. Con una trayectoria que abarca el derecho, las finanzas y el coaching, nos deja reflexiones profundas sobre los desafíos y oportunidades que enfrentamos las mujeres hoy. "Estamos tan educadas en querer ser queridas..." "Un costo siempre pagamos... la pregunta es cuál es mayor en tu vida, si ser una persona o ser personaje. Y acá no hay muchos grises." Además, nos habla sobre su más reciente libro, El viaje de la heroína (2025), y su compromiso con generar cambios reales. Mirá la entrevista completa y dejate inspirar.

programme.title: FUNDADORAS I Eli Bracciaforte: De Workana a No Pausa, liderazgo y proyectos inspiradores
programme.desc: En esta entrevista, Eliana Bracciaforte comparte su experiencia como fundadora de Workana y No Pausa, reflexiona sobre los retos de emprender desde cero, y revela cómo impulsa el crecimiento de mujeres en un mundo profesional en constante cambio. Un diálogo inspirador sobre liderazgo, aprendizajes y su compromiso con transformar la menopausia en un tema clave para el bienestar femenino.

programme.title: Afrontar la adolescencia de tus hijos, Duelo emocional de las madre, Momento de DESmadre Podcast
programme.desc: En este episodio de Momento de DESmadre, conversamos con la terapeuta familiar Erika Ángulo sobre uno de los temas más desafiantes para muchas madres: la adolescencia de los hijos y el duelo emocional que sentimos al verlos crecer y empezar a soltarse de nuestra mano. Hablamos sobre cómo manejar la etapa de la "aborrecencia", entender los cambios emocionales y de comportamiento de los adolescentes, y cómo las mamás podemos vivir este proceso sin tanta culpa, con herramientas que nos ayuden a conectar desde el amor y la empatía. Temas que tocamos: Cómo lidiar con la adolescencia de los hijos Qué es el duelo emocional en la maternidad Cambios emocionales en los adolescentes Cómo soltar y dejar crecer a los hijos sin dolor Consejos de una terapeuta familiar para madres Escucha, comparte y acompáñanos en este momento de reflexión y desahogo maternal. ¡No estás sola! Suscríbete para más conversaciones reales, sin filtros y con mucho DESmadre. #Adolescencia #MaternidadReal #PodcastParaMujeres #DueloMaternal #MomentoDeDESmadre #ErikaÁngulo #Adolescentes #Familia #PodcastEnEspañol

programme.title: MINISTERIO DE BRUJAS: Carta Astral de Los Javis, Caras de Bélmez, Mal de Ojo y Venus en Escorpio.
programme.desc: Bienvenid@s al Ministerio de Brujas, el único programa donde la magia tiene reglamento, las dudas tienen expediente y la intuición legisla sin oposición. En este episodio, grabado en vivo en@CanalBarro el aquelarre vino encendido. PROTOCOLO DE LA HOGUERA Quemamos todo lo que necesita transformarse: los crush imposibles de tu ideología opuesta, la gente que vive diciendo “no”, los silencios incómodos del WhatsApp y esa tortura mental llamada “debería estar haciendo algo”. Aquí el fuego purifica… o al menos nos da permiso para reírnos. SECRETARÍA DE VENUS EN TANGA Nos adentramos en el magnetismo oscuro de Venus en Escorpio: deseo extremo, intensidad emocional, tabúes, renacer afectivo y ese erotismo que ve en la piel ajena un archivo confidencial. Además, tiramos una carta del tarot erótico para leer el clima del deseo. DIRECCIÓN GENERAL DE CINEMATOGRAFÍA ZODIAZAL La Dra. Fernanda Garrido trae cine, signos y elementos. Películas que dialogan con el cielo y con nuestras crisis de identidad astrológica. Cine como brújula, literal. CLIMA ASTRAL & MITOS ChongaZen explica los movimientos planetarios y luego destapamos dos clásicos del misterio: • El Mal de Ojo: desde Mesopotamia hasta TikTok. • El espejo roto y los 7 años de mala suerte: Roma, magia y supersticiones que siguen vivitas. SUBSECRETARÍA DE MISTERIOS: LAS CARAS DE BÉLMEZ El caso paranormal más famoso de España: rostros que aparecen en el suelo, análisis forenses, sellos notariales, restos humanos bajo la casa y un misterio que ni la ciencia cerró. Brutal. DEPARTAMENTO DE ESTRELLAS Y SÁBANAS Analizamos la compatibilidad cósmica de Javier Calvo y Javier Ambrossi. Cartas natales sobre la mesa. La química astral nunca miente. BRUJAS QUEMADAS O EXILIADAS La activista Tarana Burke, madre del movimiento Me Too, entra en nuestros Archivos Clasificados. Poder, voz y reparación. Cierre con los Sindicatos Zodiacales Acuario pide dejar de ser llamado frí@, Cáncer pregunta si hace falta sentir TODO, y Libra… Libra reclama coherencia universal. programme.title: Unrolled
programme.desc: This episode explores Gurkha cigars' collaborative "Year of the Dragon 2024" series, featuring partnerships with master blenders and showcasing the brand's innovative packaging, promotional strategies, and dedication to the broader cigar community.

programme.title: Burn Rate
programme.sub-title: Burn Rate - Drew Estate Undercrown 10 Toro
programme.desc: On this episode of Burn Rate, hosts Bryan Baiss and Chris Kelly review the Undercrown 10 by Drew Estate Toro, evaluating its craftsmanship and flavor profile which featured dry cherry and black pepper, noting a consistently burning cigar despite its initial dryness.

programme.title: Cigar City Unrolled
programme.desc: On this episode of Unrolled, we take a look at The Cigar Castle! General Manager Rick is here to show us this unique lounge with a wide variety of selection and an impressive humidor!

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Lynn Hawkins Plasencia Cigars
programme.desc: Sean sits down with Lynn Hawkins of Placencia Cigars, one of the most respected names in the industry. Lynn pulls back the curtain on Placencia's extensive history as a leading grower and producer, sharing insights into their meticulous tobacco cultivation, the intricate art of their cigar manufacturing process, and what makes their family's legacy truly stand out in the world of premium cigars.

programme.title: Unrolled
programme.desc: In this episode of Unrolled, Sean Mobley visits Stogie Pairing Cigar Lounge in Fort Myers, Florida, where owners Joey and Jessica showcase their establishment, boasting 28 beer taps, 75 types of bottled and canned beers, and a full wine selection, emphasizing their commitment to diverse pairings for cigars.

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Rick Rodriguez West Tampa Tobacco Co
programme.desc: In this episode of "Behind the Blend," Sean Mobley interviews Rick Rodriguez, also known as "Chef Rick," from West Tampa Tobacco, who explains his nickname comes from blending tobacco like a chef uses food to create a desired flavor profile. Rick introduces new cigars like the "Circle of Life," a tribute to his mentors, and the "Double Crab," part of a Tampa-inspired trilogy, shaped like a "flying pig". He shares his personal journey into the cigar industry at age 40 and emphasizes that for him, cigars represent "connection" and a "gateway for a new friendship".

programme.title: Unrolled

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Steven Bartell Molon Labe
programme.desc: Join host Sean Mobley as he sits down with Steven Bartell, the visionary owner and founder of Molon Labe. Discover the story behind the only company in the world that combines rare reserve cigars, whiskey, and coffee all under one roof.

programme.title: Burn Rate
programme.sub-title: Burn Rate - Southern Draw Rose Of Sharon Dozen Roses Solomon
programme.desc: In this episode of "Burn Rate," hosts Bryan and Chris Kelly review the Southern Draw Rose of Sharon, Dozen Roses, a Casa de Montecristo exclusive in a Salomon vitola. They praise its craftsmanship, noting the oily, thin-veined Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper and consistent burn.

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Brian Motola And George Hadweh Cavalier
programme.desc: In this episode of "Behind the Blend," Sean Mobley interviews Brian and George from Cavalier Cigars, who discuss their roles within the company, with Brian as a partner in the Honduran factory (FBT) and George as the sales representative for Florida and Puerto Rico. Brian shares his recent full-time move to Honduras, highlighting the country's beauty and the factory's unique practice of hand-applying gold leaf to cigars, a process where empowered employees can reject imperfect products.

programme.title: Behind The Blend
programme.sub-title: Behind The Blend - Desiree Sylver Drunk Chicken
programme.desc: Established in 2019, Drunk Chicken Cigars (DC Cigars) are handmade in the U.S.A. to create premium flavor profiles. Every combination of tobacco leaf, including the filler, binder, and wrapper, was chosen to produce an assortment of smooth, rich, and savory cigars with a variety of customers in mind. Join Sean has he dicusses the mission of the DC Cigars family is to produce premium cigars that can be smoked anytime of the day.

programme.title: Gulangyu Island
programme.desc: Gulangyu Island is famous for its exotic architecture. As a key trade port in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, it was a gathering point for merchants and diplomats from all over the world. This led to a variety of architectural styles being adopted on the island, including a fusion of Chinese and Western designs, as well as some typical of the Chaozhou region. These buildings, mostly over 100 years old, stand witness to China's reconnection with the outside world.

programme.title: Suqian
programme.desc: Suqian is a small city in Jiangsu Province, which may not be so famous nowadays. In history, there was a famous figure here: Xiang Yu! Suqian is of great significance to our presenter Megan. Although she grew up in the United States, Suqian is her hometown. This time, let's follow the presenter to have a look at the local customs of her hometown that she always misses.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.3
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, traveling to the cities of Zhuzhou and Xiangtan to meet another group of extraordinary women. By capturing snippets of the lives and work of an electric locomotive designer, a flight instructor, a painter, and a poverty alleviation volunteer, we showcase the unique cultural and humanistic charm of this region.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 2
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the grand old mansions of Nanjing's merchant families and take a stroll through their exquisite gardens, where Nature is incorporated into the architecture. From centuries-old Qing Dynasty residences to traditional folk handicrafts, join us on a deep dive into Nanjing's rich cultural heritage.

programme.title: The Sea's Fruits Ep.1
programme.desc: With 18,000 kilometers of coastline, China boasts a wide range of ecosystems and a rich source of marine ingredients. The Sea's Fruits focuses on these small treasures of the sea - how they are caught, cooked, and shared. Told through stories of coming together and saying goodbye, the documentary celebrates the joy of eating and explores people's perspectives on family, friendship, and the natural world.

From centuries-old Qing Dynasty residences to traditional folk handicrafts, join us on a deep dive into Nanjing's rich cultural heritage.

programme.title: The Sea's Fruits Ep.1
programme.desc: With 18,000 kilometers of coastline, China boasts a wide range of ecosystems and a rich source of marine ingredients. The Sea's Fruits focuses on these small treasures of the sea - how they are caught, cooked, and shared. Told through stories of coming together and saying goodbye, the documentary celebrates the joy of eating and explores people's perspectives on family, friendship, and the natural world.

programme.title: Between Heaven and Earth : Traveling Through Grasslands Ep.11
programme.desc: The first season of the "Wandering the World" series follows a traveler across six of China's greatest grasslands, revealing the natural beauty of their epic landscapes and the distinctive lives of the people who inhabit them.

programme.title: Gourmets Alive II Ep.6
programme.desc: Literati such as Lu You, Li Yu, Yuan Mei, and Wang Zengqi take center stage as we explore their worlds and works through the flavors and cuisine of daily life.

programme.title: Aerial China II Ep.6
programme.desc: The mountainous realm of Fujian's centers around the Wuyi range, just opposite Taiwan Province. Join us as we trace a heritage of tea production in ancient villages, marvel at waterside Danxia, and discover terraces where seas of lotuses grow...

programme.title: Ancient melodies, modern vibes: Sang Tian's music
programme.desc: Chinese traditional music is often seen as something rooted in the past. But singer-songwriter Sang Tian is finding new ways for it to live in the present. He calls himself a "translator," fine-tuning ancient melodies into a modern musical language.

programme.title: Journey of the Chili Pepper Ep.3
programme.desc: In China, the chili pepper is an indispensable winter ingredient. Since its arrival in the Ming dynasty, the spicy staple has been reshaping Chinese food culture. Today, as a new chili craze sweeps across the nation, we’ll take a look at how the chili evolved from a simple source of heat to a fiery cultural phenomenon.

programme.title: From Farm to Table (China-France Season) Ep.5
programme.desc: Set against the backdrop of the 60th anniversary of Sino-French diplomatic relations, this program focuses on the full-chain coordination mechanism that brings food from French farms to Chinese tables, capturing the collision and fusion of two great food cultures.

programme.title: From Farm to Table (China-France Season) Ep.6
programme.desc: Set against the backdrop of the 60th anniversary of Sino-French diplomatic relations, this program focuses on the full-chain coordination mechanism that brings food from French farms to Chinese tables, capturing the collision and fusion of two great food cultures.

programme.title: Jingmai Wanderings: A Symphony of Humans and Tea
programme.desc: As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Mount Jingmai embodies the ecological wisdom of forest-tea symbiosis and the rich cultural diversity of its ethnic communities. It plays a vital role in biodiversity conservation and the preservation of traditional tea culture. This episode follows the stories of representative individuals to explore three key themes - heritage preservation, ecological sustainability, and youth empowerment - revealing the unique charm and sustainable development model of Mount Jingmai.

programme.title: China Highly Recommended: Changsha
programme.desc: Episode 1 of Travelogue's "China Highly Recommended" tells the story of Changsha, one of China's happiest cities. Following the lives of four of its foreign residents: A French executive chef, a Japanese podcaster, and two American teachers, we discover the reasons why they made Changsha their second home, and explore the city with them as only locals do. This episode will be released as a 30 minute travel documentary to be broadcast on CGTN's television channel and social media platform, along with a series of video clips and photos.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, we arrive in Changsha - the economic and cultural hub of Hunan Province, and a core city in the Yangtze River Middle Reaches Economic Zone. Our lens turns to the "Xiangjiang Ladies" who work in Changsha's high-tech and equipment manufacturing sectors. Their daily lives and professional endeavors reflect the city's innovative vitality, while their after-work gatherings also showcase the dazzling night views along both banks of the Xiangjiang River, highlighting Changsha's distinct charm as a vibrant capital of leisure and entertainment.

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 3
programme.desc: Join us in Nanjing's bustling old quarter, where you can try on silk dresses worth their weight in gold, and see how traditional handicrafts have been given modern twists. We'll feast on street snacks and local delicacies by the old Confucian Temple, before taking a pleasure cruise along Nanjing's mother river to round off our exploration of this vibrant and historic city.

programme.title: A Bite of China II Ep.1
programme.desc: In this much-anticipated sequel to the acclaimed foodie hit, we take an even closer look at the bond between Chinese people and food. Featuring around 150 characters and 300 different delicacies, we stand to witness to the role food plays in life's key moments. In short, this series offers the most flavorful insight into ancient Chinese culture that you are ever going to get!

programme.title: Gourmets Alive Ep.1
programme.desc: What did China's most celebrated scholars and poets eat? This documentary follows the trail of famous cultural figures from ancient to modern times, using reenactments to explore the classic dishes that helped define China’s rich culinary history.

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing
programme.desc: From the local delicacies of Beijing's Ox Street to latest hangouts and contemporary cuisine of the Chinese capital, hosts Tianran He and Eva May will give you a true taste of Beijing, and the fascinating stories and people behind them.

programme.title: Foodwise: Qingdao
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May venture to Qingdao, China's beer mecca by the sea. With red tiles and green trees that make up the city's stunning scenery, our hosts embark on another foodie-journey with local delicacies and interesting guest appearances. From drinking beer with a German friend, catching crabs by the ocean and devouring grilled eel the classic Korean way, this episode will leave you hungry for more!

programme.title: The Qibao Ancient Town
programme.desc: Pudong reflects the changes of Shanghai over the past ten years, the Bund represents Shanghai's hundred‑year history, and Qibao Ancient Town bears witness to Shanghai's thousand years of vicissitudes. To support the publicity for the first China International Import Expo in Shanghai, we come to Qibao Ancient Town, a rare surviving ancient town within Shanghai's urban area, close to Hongqiao Airport and the site of the Import Expo. We recommend this destination for short‑term travellers. Transportation here is very convenient, and you can experience the charm of traditional Shanghai.

programme.title: Fearless Journey Ep.1
programme.desc: Ten outdoor enthusiasts take on the world through various sports ---- from marathons to cycling ---- experiencing geography, culture, history, and the spirit of athletics.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But there's more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise. Kleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan's narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals.

programme.title: Living Arts of Huizhou
programme.desc: This is Huangshan in eastern China. In this city, you'll encounter one of China's most traditional building styles: Hui-style architecture. How does Hui style set this region apart? What's life like for people living in these houses? With these questions in mind, we're embarking on a journey to decode Hui-style architecture.

programme.title: Colors of the Daliang Mountains
programme.desc: In the first episode of our Sichuan Daliang Mountains series, we journey to Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture in Sichuan Province. Setting off from Xichang, the prefectural capital, we first explore Lizhou Ancient Town, the southern gateway of the Southern Silk Road. We then travel to Huili County in the southernmost part of the Daliang Mountains, where we listen to the morning bells and evening drums, try our hand at making green pottery, and pick fresh pomegranates. Finally, we head to the western part of the Greater Liangshan Mountains and step into the mysterious Lugu Lake. We visit a Mosuo family to learn about their unique culture and take part in one of the Mosuo people's most important rituals: the coming of age ceremony.

programme.title: Aerial China III Ep.1
programme.desc: Yunnan straddles the Hengduan Mountains and Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau, revealing Kawagarbo Peak, vibrant Lijiang, and Hani's golden terraces. Come fly with us on a quest for the essence of Yunnan and discover why it so richly deserves its name - Yunnan, 'the Land South of the Clouds'!

programme.title: Chinese for a Day | intro
programme.desc: In this episode, we travel to Shanxi Province, one of the birthplaces of Chinese civilization. Jack and Jonathan discover 4,000-year-old artifacts and explore how ancient Chinese people used astronomy to mark the seasons, uncovering the wisdom and traditions of an ancient civilization.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But there's more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise. Kleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan's narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals.

programme.title: Gourmets Alive Ep.2
programme.desc: What did China's most celebrated scholars and poets eat? This documentary follows the trail of famous cultural figures from ancient to modern times, using reenactments to explore the classic dishes that helped define China’s rich culinary history.

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing's Hutongs
programme.desc: The Hutongs in Beijing are considered the city's blood vessels, as these traditional alleyways make up the DNA of the capital for its rich history and culture. In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May zigzag their way through the Hutongs and the Forbidden City for a mouth-watering experience full of ancient and modern delicacies. Starring German designer Katrin, Russian artist Liuba and photographer Feng Yu from Beijing, our hosts are taking you along a journey that features fried noodles, dim sum, pancakes and co.!

programme.title: Foodwise: Datong
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Angela Fu are in historic Datong. Located in northern China's Shanxi Province, some 1500 years ago Datong was the capital of the Northern Wei Dynasty, which saw nomads unite northern China and Buddhism spread throughout the country. At the renowned Yungang Grottoes where giant Buddhas were carved out of cliffs, our hosts discover Datong's multicultural past and sample the emperor's favorite cake. They seek out the remains of a Jesuit church beneath the Great Wall of China, and find in the local cuisine elements that echo the past, and modern-day recipes for thousand-year old dishes.

programme.title: The Spirit of Wuhan
programme.desc: In this episode, we arrive at Wuhan, the River City known as the "Thoroughfare of Nine Provinces". We take the audience to visit the time‑honoured Yellow Crane Tower, the time‑defying Zhiyin Hao, and the romantic, nostalgic Lihuangpi Road. We listen to well‑loved excerpts from classic Chu Opera and sample authentic local delicacies. Through these small moments, we showcase Wuhan's unique cultural charm and local features.

programme.title: Fearless Journey Ep.2
programme.desc: Ten outdoor enthusiasts take on the world through various sports ---- from marathons to cycling ---- experiencing geography, culture, history, and the spirit of athletics.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Pak Mei
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber seeks out Liu Weixin, a master of Pak Mei kungfu and on whom the hit game "Sifu" was based. He experiences for himself this style's relentless and lightning-fast strikes, but also learns from its master how to balance life and kungfu, how a master should treat his disciples, and what it means to "eat porridge at night".

programme.title: Fujian's Tulou - The Mysterious Earthen Castles
programme.desc: The tulous, or earth-built dwellings, of Fujian are recognized as treasures of traditional architecture, thanks to their unique design, cultural importance, and embodiment of the concept of harmonious coexistence with nature. Tulous are mostly rectangular or circular in form, with a simple, elegant exterior and a well-furnished interior. As homes built by the Hakka people, they are imbued with diligence, wisdom, and the pursuit of excellence. Surrounded by mountains and waters, the tulous blend well with the natural environment. When building their tulous, the Hakka people pay attention to ecological balance in order to minimize their environmental footprint. A tulou is not only a safe place to live, but also the crystallization of the culture and architectural skill passed down for generations among the Hakka people.

programme.title: Fiery Tales of the Daliang Mountains
programme.desc: In this episode, our host takes you to Liangshan Yi Autonomous Prefecture in Sichuan Province, to celebrate the most traditional Torch Festival with the local Yi people. Water nourishes the farmland; fire brings light and warmth. Water and fire are the two essential elements that sustain the life of the Yi people. Puge County is known as the birthplace of the Yi Torch Festival. Our host travels across mountains to the remote heart of Puge County, in search of the origins of the Yi torch, to learn about local daily life, explore the profound Yi culture, and visit a Yi family to share a special "reunion dinner" on the eve of the Torch Festival - just like their own New Year's Eve feast. Together with the locals, we celebrate their most magnificent festival: the Torch Festival.

programme.title: Foodwise: Eating Global in Beijing
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May are in search of global cuisines that can be found in Beijing, the 3000-year old capital of China. From honest farm-to-table fare, to the culinary heights of French haute cuisine, and even a cooking class and wine and dine event at a traditional courtyard home in the city center, we'll discover that in Beijing, you can taste the world.

programme.title: Foodwise: Chaozhou
programme.desc: In this episode, hosts Tianran He and Angela Fu are in Chaozhou, South China. They're on a quest to discover the secrets of its success, for Chaozhou is famed for its wealthy merchant guilds and its homegrown Teochew cuisine, which enjoys global recognition. From working as part-timers in a beef hotpot restaurant, to learning about tea ceremony and shadowing a master of Teochew cuisine, our hosts discover the best way to learn about Chaozhou, is through its food.

programme.title: Mystical Zhangjiajie
